## blocking-restriction

Blocks **4** cards.

- **(keyword)** the same missing block-legality hook as Stromkirk Noble (filtered by creature type) and Vampire Cutthroat (filtered by relative power), here filtered by color and card type: the `intimidate` evasion keyword -- "this creature can't be blocked except by artifact creatures and/or creatures that share a color with it" -- as a `Keyword` enum member the loader accepts, plus the block-legality rule behind it in `combat.py`: a declared blocker is legal only if it has the Artifact type OR its colors intersect the attacker's colors. It must read *derived* colors of both creatures at declare-blockers time, so a creature that has been made black can block this and this creature being made a second color widens who may block it
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `Keyword` (`engine/enums.py:131-153`) is a closed enum of 15 members and `KNOWN_KEYWORDS` is derived from it (`cards/loader.py:37`), so a card printing `intimidate` in its `keywords` or granting it via `grant_keyword` is a `DslError` at load, not a silent no-op. Nothing in the list is a colour-based evasion: `EVASION_KEYWORDS` is exactly `{flying, menace}` (`enums.py:156`) and `combat.py:181` notes menace is the only blocking restriction implemented. Menace is the nearest and is wrong in both directions -- it permits any two creatures of any colour to block, and forbids a lone artifact creature or a lone black creature from blocking, which intimidate expressly allows. `protection` (the one parameterised static, with `from_colors`) is a stop rather than an exemption: it names colours that *may not* block and it also blanks damage, targeting and enchanting, whereas intimidate names the colours that *may* and touches nothing but blocking -- and its `from_colors` is a fixed literal list, so it cannot say "shares a color with THIS creature" and would have to be rewritten if the creature's colour changed
- **(static_effect)** a static continuous effect that restricts which creatures may block the source, filtered by a characteristic of the would-be blocker (here `subtypes: ["Human"]`) -- i.e. an evasion effect of the form "this creature can't be blocked by <filter>", evaluated when blockers are declared rather than as a granted keyword
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `static_effects` offers only `buff`, `grant_keyword`, `set_pt`, `add_subtype` and `extra_land_drops` -- all of which change characteristics of permanents, none of which constrains the legality of a block. The nearest keyword is `menace` (and `flying`/`reach`), but those are fixed evasion rules with no filter: menace requires two or more blockers of any type and would let a single Human block alongside a second creature, while this card must forbid Humans outright and permit any one non-Human blocker. `static_filter_keys` does contain `blocking` and `subtypes`, but a filter alone has no restriction effect to attach to -- there is no effect kind that consumes it to veto a block declaration.
- **(static_effect)** A static effect that constrains how a creature may be blocked, evaluated when blocks are declared and again when they are validated as a set. Tromokratis needs the 'all creatures the defending player controls must be blocking this creature, or the block is illegal' variant, which is a whole-declaration legality check rather than a per-pair one; the same effect should cover the ordinary 'can't be blocked' and 'can't be blocked except by N or more creatures' cases.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: The only static effects available are buff, grant_keyword, set_pt, add_subtype and extra_land_drops -- none of them speaks about blocking at all. The nearest existing thing is the menace keyword, but it is a fixed hardcoded rule rather than a parameterised one: combat.blocks_valid is documented as 'Menace is the only one implemented' and hardcodes len(blockers) < 2, and combat.can_block only knows about tapped/controller/protection, so there is no seam where a card-supplied blocking restriction could be consulted. Granting menace instead would be an approximation (2 blockers, not all of them) and is refused.
- **(static_effect)** The same missing capability filed for `stromkirk_noble`: a static continuous effect that vetoes a block declaration against its source, filtered by a characteristic of the would-be blocker, consulted from `engine/combat.py:can_block` when blockers are declared. Skulk needs a *distinct sub-need* on top of that: the filter is not a fixed quality but a RELATIVE COMPARISON between two objects -- "power of the would-be blocker > power of this creature", read from derived (not printed) power on both sides at the moment blockers are declared, so an anthem, a pump spell or a +1/+1 counter on either creature changes who may block. Concretely this wants either (a) a `skulk` entry in `Keyword`/`EVASION_KEYWORDS` handled directly in `can_block`, or (b) a general "can't be blocked by" static whose filter may express a comparison against a characteristic of the source -- e.g. a value expression like `{"power_of": "source"}` usable as the right-hand side of the selector's `power: {"op": ">", "value": ...}` comparison.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `Keyword` is a closed enum of fifteen (`src/automtg/engine/enums.py:131`) with no `skulk`, and `EVASION_KEYWORDS` is `frozenset({FLYING, MENACE})` -- an unknown keyword is a load-time `DslError`, not a silently inert card. `can_block` (`src/automtg/engine/combat.py:121-153`) consults exactly three restrictions: protection, flying-vs-reach, and (via `blocks_valid`) menace; nothing reads a static there. `STATIC_EFFECTS` (`src/automtg/cards/loader.py:41-71`) offers `buff`, `grant_keyword`, `set_pt`, `add_subtype`, `set_types`, `protection` and the player-wide ones -- every object-facing one changes a characteristic, none constrains block legality. `protection` is the only static `can_block` does read, but it is wrong twice over: it names a fixed quality (`from_types`/`from_subtypes`/`from_colors`) and cannot express a power comparison at all, and it is a DEBT keyword that would also stop damage, enchanting and targeting, making the creature far better than the one printed. `menace` restricts blocker *count*, not blocker power. Filter keys cannot reach it either: `STATIC_FILTER_KEYS` (`loader.py:76-97`) has no `power` key whatsoever, and even the full selector's `power: {"op": ">", "value": {...}}` compares against a value expression with no way to name the blocked creature's own power -- `power_of` takes a `var` (snapshot) or a `target`, and a static block restriction has neither. Static filters are additionally required to read only *printed* characteristics, which skulk must not do.

## attack-requirement

Blocks **3** cards.

- **(op)** an effect op that places an until-end-of-turn 'attacks this combat if able' requirement on a set of creatures chosen by an ordinary selector (here `{"zone": "battlefield", "controller": "opponent", "types": ["Creature"], "count": "all"}`), surviving on creatures that were not on the battlefield when it resolved only if the printed card says so (Bident's does not, so a snapshot of the affected set at resolution is correct)
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: The whole Board/Modify op groups act on characteristics or on the object's own state: `tap`, `freeze` and `skip_untap` stop a permanent from being available, and `lock_abilities` removes a permission, but none of them can *compel* an action. `lock_abilities` is the closest in spirit — an until-end-of-turn, non-keyword permission flag read by legality — yet it is a prohibition read at activation time, and an attack requirement is an obligation read while declaring attackers, so it cannot be spelled as a negation of anything that exists.
- **(engine)** the declare-attackers step must enforce requirements: a legal attack declaration has to include every creature under a requirement that is able to attack (untapped, not summoning sick, no defender), and the AI/agent choosing attackers for the affected player must be constrained to a maximal legal set rather than being free to decline
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: Nothing in the reference vocabulary reaches combat declaration at all — `attacks` and `blocks` exist only as trigger events that observe a declaration that has already been made, and `defending` merely reads who was attacked. An op that recorded the flag with no enforcement would load, show on the board and change nothing, which is the exact failure mode the format exists to refuse.
- **(static_effect)** the same requirement as a continuous form, so the many printed variants ('Creatures your opponents control attack each combat if able', 'Enchanted creature attacks each combat if able') and full goad ('attacks each combat if able and attacks a player other than you if able') share one enforcement point in the declare-attackers check
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `static_effects` is limited to `buff`, `grant_keyword`, `set_pt`, `add_subtype`, `set_types`, `extra_land_drops` and the player-wide seven, all of which write characteristics or player permissions that the characteristics pipeline reads. `grant_keyword` cannot stand in: the engine's keyword list is a fixed vocabulary of fifteen and an attack requirement is a behaviour, not a printed characteristic, so granting a keyword would need the same combat-step enforcement to exist first.
- **(static_effect)** a continuous static effect meaning 'each creature matched by `affects` attacks each combat if able', so that the printed variants ('This creature attacks each combat if able', 'Creatures your opponents control attack each combat if able', 'Enchanted creature attacks each combat if able') are one effect with one enforcement point. For this card it would read `{"kind": "static", "effect": "attacks_if_able", "affects": {"self_only": true}}`.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: The static effect vocabulary is `buff`, `grant_keyword`, `set_pt`, `add_subtype`, `set_types` plus the player-wide seven, and every one of them writes a characteristic or a player permission that the characteristics pipeline reads. An attack requirement is an obligation on a future action, not a characteristic. `grant_keyword` is the nearest fit and cannot stand in: the keyword vocabulary is a closed list of fifteen (`deathtouch` ... `vigilance`), and even if a `must_attack` keyword were added to it, granting it would change nothing until the declare-attackers step read it. `defender` is the only combat-shaped keyword and it is the exact opposite -- a prohibition on attacking, enforced by refusing an attacker, whereas this must force one in.
- **(engine)** declare-attackers must enforce requirements: an attack declaration is legal only if it includes every creature under a requirement that is able to attack (untapped, not summoning sick, no `defender`, not otherwise restricted), and the agent choosing attackers for that player must be constrained to such a set rather than being free to decline.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: Nothing in the DSL reaches combat declaration. `attacks` and `blocks` are trigger events that observe a declaration already made, and `defending` only reads who was attacked; `tap`, `freeze`, `skip_untap` and `lock_abilities` all remove availability or permission and none can compel an action. Without this half, a static that merely recorded the flag would load, look implemented and do nothing -- the failure this format exists to refuse. This is the same engine need already filed under `attack_requirement` for Bident of Thassa; that card wants the one-shot until-end-of-turn form, this one wants the permanent form, and both want this enforcement point.
- **(static_effect)** an 'unless' clause on the requirement -- a static whose applicability is re-checked against board state, here `{"not": {"exists": {"zone": "battlefield", "controller": "you", "types": ["Creature"], "name": "Advocate of the Beast"}}}`. Either a static `condition` that accepts the ordinary condition language, or an `unless` selector on the attack-requirement effect itself.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: A static's `condition` is deliberately tiny: `characteristics._static_condition_met` reads only `condition.counters`, i.e. how many counters of one kind sit on the static's own source, so it cannot ask about another permanent at all. Widening it generally would let one static depend on another's output and break the acyclic fixed-order pipeline, so the requirement's own effect is the safer place to carry an `unless` selector. Note that matching a permanent by name is NOT the blocker: `name` is already in `SELECTOR_KEYS` and works in ordinary selectors and in `exists` conditions. It is absent from `STATIC_FILTER_KEYS`, but that list constrains `affects`, and the name test belongs in the condition, not in `affects`.
- **(op)** an effect op that places an attack requirement on a single targeted creature -- `{"op": "must_attack", "target": {"zone": "battlefield", "controller": "opponent", "types": ["Creature"]}, "duration": "next_combat"}` -- meaning 'this creature attacks during its controller's next combat phase if able'. The duration is the part not shared with the already-filed variants: it is neither until-end-of-turn (Bident of Thassa) nor permanent (Marauding Maulhorn), but a one-shot obligation that persists across turns until that player's *next* combat phase arrives, is discharged there, and expires whether or not the creature was able to attack.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: No op in the vocabulary can compel an action. `tap`, `freeze` and `skip_untap` remove availability, `lock_abilities` removes a permission -- all prohibitions, and an attack requirement cannot be spelled as the negation of any of them. `delay` is the closest fit for the timing half and still does not help: it schedules an *effect* to run at a later step, whereas this must install a requirement that the declare-attackers legality check reads, and `delay` has nothing to run because no such requirement exists. Duplicating this as a bare 'this turn' op would also be wrong here -- the trigger fires on the controller's own landfall, so 'this turn' would frequently be discharged during a combat phase the affected opponent never gets.
- **(engine)** declare-attackers must enforce requirements: an attack declaration is legal only if it includes every creature under an unexpired requirement that is able to attack (untapped, not summoning sick, no `defender`, not otherwise restricted), and the agent choosing attackers for that player must be constrained to such a set rather than being free to decline. For the `next_combat` duration this is also the point where the obligation is discharged and cleared.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: Nothing in the DSL reaches combat declaration. `attacks` and `blocks` are trigger events that observe a declaration already made. Without this half, an op that merely recorded the flag would load, claim the printed line and change nothing -- the exact failure this format exists to refuse. This is the same engine need already filed under `attack_requirement` for Bident of Thassa and Marauding Maulhorn; all three want this one enforcement point, and this card additionally needs it to expire a per-combat obligation there.

## static-condition

Blocks **3** cards.

- **(static_effect)** an "as long as..." condition on a static ability that may read game state other than counters on its own source -- at minimum a `cmp` over a life total -- so a static's buff and keyword grant can switch on and off with the board. Whatever form it takes has to declare its evaluation order in the characteristics pipeline, since the current restriction exists to keep that pipeline acyclic
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `_validate_static_condition` (`cards/loader.py:504-515`) rejects any static `condition` that is not exactly `{"counters": ...}` -- one key, asking how many counters of a kind sit on the source -- and `docs/card-dsl.md` ("As long as...") states the same limit and the reason for it: a condition reading a derived characteristic would let one static depend on another static's output. A life total is not a counter and is not on this permanent, so there is no spelling of this condition that loads. The `if` EFFECT's condition language is far richer, but it is unreachable here: `if` is an op, ops run inside `spell_effects` or an ability's `effects`, and a static ability has neither -- its parameters are flattened onto the ability and the characteristics pipeline never runs the effect interpreter. Nor can a trigger substitute: `permanent_enters`/`upkeep` plus a `pump` would apply the bonus once at a moment in time and keep it until cleanup, while the printed card gains AND LOSES +2/+1 the instant the life total crosses 10 in either direction, including mid-combat
- **(static_effect)** an "as long as..." condition on a static ability that may read game state other than counters on its own source -- for THIS card specifically, a count of cards in a zone belonging to a player, i.e. `{"cmp": ">=", "left": {"count": {"zone": "graveyard", "controller": "you"}}, "right": {"const": 7}}` or an equivalent threshold form -- so a static `buff` switches on and off as the graveyard crosses seven cards. This is the ability word `Threshold`, shared by a large slice of Odyssey-block cards, so the condition wants to be general rather than a bespoke `threshold: true` flag. Whatever form it takes must declare its place in the fixed-order characteristics pipeline, since the present restriction exists to keep that pipeline acyclic; a zone count is board state and cannot depend on another static's output, so it is safe in the same way `attached` is.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `_validate_static_condition` (src/automtg/cards/loader.py:504-524) rejects any static `condition` whose key set is not exactly `{"counters"}`, and `characteristics._static_condition_met` (src/automtg/engine/characteristics.py:188-198) reads only `condition.counters` -- how many counters of one kind sit on the static's own source. `docs/card-dsl.md` ("As long as...") states the same limit. Cards in a graveyard are not counters and are not on this permanent, so no condition spelling loads. The alternative route, a `{"count": filter}` static value, is closed twice over: static values are restricted to `{"const": n}` and `{"count": filter}` (`_validate_static_value`), the count filter is restricted to `STATIC_FILTER_KEYS`, and `zone` is NOT in that frozenset (loader.py:76-97) -- so a static can only count battlefield permanents, never graveyard cards. Even given a `zone` key it would be the wrong shape: `{"count": ...}` is linear, giving +N/+N for N cards, while the printed card is a step function that is +0/+0 at six cards and +2/+2 at seven. The `if` op's condition language is richer and does have `cmp` plus zone-aware `exists`, but it is unreachable here: `if` is an op, ops run only inside `spell_effects` or an ability's `effects`, and a static ability has neither -- its parameters are flattened onto the ability and the characteristics pipeline never invokes the effect interpreter. A triggered ability cannot substitute either: a `pump` from `upkeep` or `creature_dies` applies a bonus at a moment and holds it until cleanup, whereas the printed bonus appears AND disappears the instant the graveyard crosses seven in either direction, including mid-combat and including when cards leave the graveyard -- and no trigger event in the list (`dies`, `creature_dies`, `draw`, `mill` has none) fires on every card entering or leaving a graveyard anyway.
- **(static_effect)** an "as long as..." condition on a static ability that may read something other than counters on its own source -- here, a player-level predicate ("as long as you have the city's blessing"), so that `{"kind": "static", "effect": "grant_keyword", "affects": {"self_only": true}, "keywords": ["flying"]}` can switch on and off with the blessing. Whatever form it takes must declare its place in the fixed-order characteristics pipeline; a player-level predicate is actually the EASY case for that, since the blessing is player state rather than a derived characteristic and so cannot make one static depend on another static's output
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `_validate_static_condition` (`src/automtg/cards/loader.py:504-524`) raises `DslError` on any static `condition` whose key set is not exactly `{"counters"}`, and within that the only permitted keys are `counter`, `amount` and `op` -- i.e. the one question "how many counters of this kind sit on my own source". `docs/card-dsl.md` ("As long as...") states the same limit and its reason. "You have the city's blessing" is not a counter and is not on this permanent, so there is no spelling of this condition that loads. The richer condition language (`cmp`, `all`, `any`, `not`, `exists`, `zone_is`, `is_your_turn`) belongs to the `if` OP and is unreachable from a static: ops run inside `spell_effects` or an ability's `effects`, and a static ability has neither -- its parameters are flattened onto the ability and the characteristics pipeline never runs the effect interpreter. Granting the keyword from a trigger is not a substitute either: `grant_keyword` as an effect is an until-end-of-turn grant on a discrete event, whereas the printed line is a permanent conditional characteristic that must be true the moment the blessing is gained, including mid-combat and on an opponent's turn. Note this item is blocked SECOND, behind `ascend` above -- even with the condition language widened there is currently no blessing for it to ask about, and even with the blessing implemented this static could not consult it

## exile-until-leaves

Blocks **2** cards.

- **(engine)** a persistent link recorded when a permanent exiles something -- on the exiler or on the exiled object -- naming which cards this source exiled, written by `exile` and readable by a later, separate resolution of a `leaves_battlefield` ability on the same source. Same one link Oblivion Ring, Banishing Light, Fiend Hunter and Angel of Sanctions all wait on; already filed on `data/authoring/gaps/oblivion_ring.json` under this exact capability slug
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `snapshot` is documented as the answer to last-known information, but it writes into `EffectContext.bindings`, which lives for exactly one resolution. The `self_enters` trigger that exiles and the `leaves_battlefield` trigger that would return are two separate abilities with two separate contexts, so a snapshot taken by the first is gone before the second runs. `exile` itself takes only `objects` and records nothing about who exiled what -- `zones.exile` just moves the object with `cause="exiled"` -- so once the Angel has left there is nothing anywhere saying which card in exile was hers. `delay` is the one op whose bindings are captured at scheduling time, but its `step` vocabulary is `upkeep`/`draw_step`/`begin_combat`/`end_step`, turn-based moments, not "when this permanent leaves".
- **(selector)** a selector key naming the cards exiled by the source permanent, e.g. `{"zone": "exile", "exiled_with": "self"}`, resolvable from a `leaves_battlefield` trigger after the source has already gone
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `SELECTOR_KEYS` in `src/automtg/engine/effects/selectors.py` has no exile-linkage key (`zone`, `controller`, types/subtypes/colors/keywords, p/t/mana_value comparisons, `exclude_self`, `self_only`, `count`, `chooser`, `random`, `target`, `binding`, `object_kind`, `name`, `damaged`). `{"target": "t1"}` only reaches targets of the ability currently resolving, and `{"binding": ...}` only reaches that resolution's bindings -- a `leaves_battlefield` trigger binds `subject`, `self` and `was_attacking`, none of which is the exiled card. The only selector that reaches exile at all is a plain `{"zone": "exile", ...}` filter, which matches every card in exile from every source, so returning over it would hand back cards the Angel never exiled. That is a different card, not an approximation of this one.
- **(engine)** a persistent link recorded on the exiling permanent (or on the exiled object) naming which cards it exiled, written by `exile` and readable by a later, separate ability resolution of the same permanent - the O-Ring / Banishing Light / Fiend Hunter family all need exactly this one link
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `snapshot` is the documented answer to last-known information, but it writes into `EffectContext.bindings`, which lives only for one resolution: the `self_enters` trigger and the `leaves_battlefield` trigger are two separate abilities with two separate contexts, so a snapshot taken by the first is gone before the second runs. `exile` itself takes only `objects` and stores nothing about who exiled what (`zones.exile` just calls `move_object` with `cause="exiled"`), so after the enchantment leaves there is nothing anywhere that says which card in exile was its victim.
- **(selector)** a selector key that names the cards exiled by the source permanent, e.g. `{"zone": "exile", "exiled_with": "self"}`, resolvable from a `leaves_battlefield` trigger after the source has already left the battlefield
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `SELECTOR_KEYS` has no exile-linkage key. `{"target": "t1"}` only reaches targets chosen for the ability currently resolving, and `{"binding": ...}` only reaches that resolution's bindings - the leaves trigger binds `subject`, `self` and `was_attacking`, none of which is the exiled card. The only selector that reaches exile at all is a plain `{"zone": "exile", ...}` filter, which matches every card in exile from every source, so `put_onto_battlefield` over it would return cards this enchantment never exiled. That is a different card, not an approximation of this one.
- **(trigger_event)** `leaves_battlefield` with `source: "self"` needs to carry the source's exile link into the trigger's bindings at the moment the permanent leaves, the way `was_attacking` is snapshotted for an object that has already gone
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `leaves_battlefield` fires correctly with `source: "self"`, but its bindings are built fresh per trigger and carry no memory of what the permanent did while it was on the battlefield. `delay` is the one op whose bindings are captured early, and its `step` vocabulary is `upkeep`/`draw_step`/`begin_combat`/`end_step` - turn-based moments, not "when this permanent leaves" - so it cannot schedule the return either.

## flashback

Blocks **2** cards.

- **(cost)** A card-level `flashback` field carrying a full alternative cost (mana `{1}{U}` plus `pay_life: 3`) that legality offers only for a copy of the card in its owner's graveyard, replacing the printed mana cost rather than adding to it
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `retrace` is the only field that widens legality to scan the graveyard (legality._cast_actions loops `state.players[pid].graveyard` on `card.retrace`), but it is a bare boolean: `CardDef.retrace_cost` is hardcoded to `Cost(discard=1, discard_selector={'types': ['Land']})` and `game.py` charges it *in addition* to the printed `{3}{U}`, so it can express neither a cheaper alternative mana cost nor a life payment as part of the alternative cost. `kicker` is a string cost but is an additional cost paid from the hand and never changes which zone a card may be cast from. `suspend` names an alternative cost but plays the card from exile after a counter countdown, not from the graveyard on demand. Cycling -- newly shipped as `Cost.discard_self` plus `active_zones` on an activated ability -- is the closest new arrival and is still the wrong shape twice over: it *activates* an ability rather than *casting* the card, so the spell never goes on the stack and `spell_effects` never run and the draw would have to be duplicated into the ability; and loader.py:326 requires any ability active outside the battlefield to pay `discard_self`, i.e. to remove its source from that zone by discarding, which a graveyard card cannot do. Cost already carries `pay_life`, so the life half exists; what is missing is any way to attach a whole alternative cost to a graveyard *cast*.
- **(replacement)** A once-only rider on that alternative cast: when the spell resolves (or is countered) it goes to exile instead of the graveyard, so the card cannot be flashed back a second time
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `retrace` deliberately returns the card to the graveyard and is reusable every turn, which is the opposite of flashback's once-only exile. Nothing else can substitute: the `replacements` whitelist is only `self_enters`, `self_enters_tapped` and `self_enters_with_counters`, so no card can replace a spell's move to the graveyard; and the `exile` op in `spell_effects` cannot stand in for it, because it would run on every cast including the first from hand, exiling the card before it could ever be flashed back.
- **(cost)** A card-level `flashback` field carrying an alternative mana cost (`{7}{W}{W}`) that legality offers only for a copy of the card in its owner's graveyard, replacing the printed `{3}{W}{W}` rather than adding to it, plus the once-only rider that the spell goes to exile instead of the graveyard when it resolves or is countered
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `retrace` is the only field that widens legality to scan the graveyard (`legality._cast_actions` loops `state.players[pid].graveyard` on `card.retrace`), but it is a bare boolean: `CardDef.retrace_cost` is hardcoded to `Cost(discard=1, discard_selector={'types': ['Land']})` and `game.py` charges it *in addition* to the printed cost, so it can name no alternative mana cost at all — Increasing Devotion would cost `{3}{W}{W}` plus a discarded land instead of `{7}{W}{W}`. Retrace is also deliberately reusable, returning the card to the graveyard, which is the opposite of flashback's exile. `kicker` is a real string cost but is additional, paid from the hand, and never changes which zone a card may be cast from. `suspend` names an alternative cost but plays the card from exile on a counter countdown, not from the graveyard on demand. The `replacements` whitelist covers only enters-the-battlefield shapes, so nothing can replace a spell's move to the graveyard, and an `exile` op in `spell_effects` cannot stand in because it would fire on the first cast from hand too, exiling the card before it could ever be flashed back. Same need filed under this slug for Deep Analysis (`data/authoring/gaps/deep_analysis.json`), which additionally needs a `pay_life` component in the alternative cost; Increasing Devotion needs only the mana half, so one field satisfying both is a full cost, not just a mana string.
- **(value)** A condition readable inside `if`, of the shape `{"cast_from_graveyard": true}` (equivalently `{"flashed_back": true}`), that is true exactly when the resolving spell was cast from its owner's graveyard — so one card can do strictly more on the flashback cast than on the cast from hand, without duplicating the card
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `{"kicked": true}` is precisely this shape and precisely this plumbing — a per-cast flag chosen on the action, carried through `stack.push_spell(..., kicked=action.kicked)` onto `EffectContext.kicked`, and read in `conditions.evaluate` — but it is welded to the `kicker` cost, and the loader actively rejects a `kicked` condition on a card with no `kicker` (`loader.py:215`), so it cannot be borrowed to mean anything else. `zone_is` reads `ctx.state.objects[ctx.source_oid].zone` — the source's *current* zone, which for any resolving sorcery is the stack, identically whether it was cast from hand or from the graveyard, so it cannot tell the two casts apart. No selector, value expression or binding records a spell's cast-from zone either. Note this need is distinct from the cost need above and does not fall out of it: an engine could implement flashback casting completely and this card would still be unimplementable, because it would create five tokens on the flashback cast instead of ten.

## player-quantifier

Blocks **2** cards.

- **(value)** the existential over individual opponents already specified in the Vampire Lacerator gap record -- `min_life_of` / `max_life_of` over a multi-player spec, or the general `{"any_player": {"players": "each_opponent", "condition": {...}}}` condition form -- so that "an opponent has 10 or less life" is a question about SOME ONE opponent. Needed here in whatever condition language the `static_condition` item above ends up with, not only in the `if`-effect language
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `life_of` is the only way to read a life total and it SUMS over its player spec (`engine/effects/values.py:102-104` does `sum(ctx.state.players[p].life for p in pids)`), while `"opponent"` and `"each_opponent"` are the same thing -- `select_players` returns `ctx.opponents()` for both. So even granting the `static_condition` item above, `{"cmp": "<=", "left": {"life_of": "opponent"}, "right": {"const": 10}}` would read "my opponents' COMBINED life is 10 or less". In a duel that matches the printed card; in a pod it is a different card, and the wrong way round -- three opponents at 4 life each sum to 12, so this creature would stay a 1/1 against a table that is nearly dead. This engine is multiplayer and this repo is Commander-first, so that is a divergence rather than a rounding error. `min`/`max` exist as value expressions but take a literal list of value expressions, and no player spec enumerates opponents one at a time to feed them
- **(value)** per-player aggregate value expressions over a multi-player spec -- `min_life_of` / `max_life_of` (and the same shape for other player quantities such as cards in hand), so `{"min_life_of": "each_opponent"}` yields the life total of the opponent who has the least rather than a total across opponents. With that, "an opponent has 10 or less life" is `{"cmp": "<=", "left": {"min_life_of": "each_opponent"}, "right": {"const": 10}}`
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `life_of` is the only way to read a life total and it SUMS over its player spec (`values.py:104` does `sum(ctx.state.players[p].life for p in pids)`), and `"opponent"` is a plain alias for `"each_opponent"` -- `select_players` (`selectors.py:278-279`) returns `ctx.opponents()` for both. So `{"life_of": "opponent"} <= 10` reads as "my opponents' COMBINED life is 10 or less", which is identical to the printed card in a duel but diverges sharply in a pod: three opponents at 40 sum to 120, so the exemption becomes effectively unreachable and the card applies its own drawback in games where the real one would not. `min`/`max` exist as value expressions but take a list of value expressions, and there is no per-opponent player spec to feed them -- the player specs are `you`, `opponent`/`each_opponent`, `each_player`, `active_player`, `{target}`, `{controller_of}`, `{owner_of}`, `{binding}`, none of which enumerates opponents one at a time
- **(op)** a quantifier over players in the condition DSL -- `{"any_player": {"players": "each_opponent", "condition": {...}}}` and its `each_player` counterpart -- evaluating the inner condition once per selected player and OR-ing (resp. AND-ing) the results, so "an opponent has 10 or less life" and "each opponent has 10 or less life" become distinguishable. This is the general form; the `min_life_of` value above is the narrow special case
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: the condition DSL (`conditions.py`, CONDITION_KEYS = cmp/all/any/not/exists/zone_is/is_your_turn/kicked) has no player-scoped form at all. `all`/`any` combine a fixed literal list of sub-conditions written into the card, not a list generated per player, so they cannot range over an opponent count that is unknown until the game is set up. `exists` looks the closest but quantifies over OBJECTS -- it calls `resolve_pool` on an object selector -- and there is no player selector to hand it. `{"controller_of": "snapshot_name"}` does yield a single player, but it is whichever one arbitrary opponent happens to control the snapshotted permanent, and an opponent controlling nothing is invisible to it, so it cannot express "any opponent"

Meloku differs from Trench Behemoth in one way worth building for: the returned land is combined with a mana cost (`{1}`), so the new component must compose with `mana` in the same `Cost`, not stand alone. Note also that the cost is repeatable with no tap, so payability must be re-tested per activation as the land pool shrinks.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `Cost` (`engine/carddef.py:37-55`, mirrored by `CostModel` in `cards/schema.py:18-35`) carries exactly `mana`, `tap`, `untap`, `sacrifice`, `discard`, `discard_selector`, `discard_self`, `pay_life`, `remove_counters` and `exile_from_graveyard`; nothing in that list moves a battlefield permanent to hand. `sacrifice` is the closest -- same selector shape, same ask-the-player payment -- but it puts the land in the graveyard instead of the hand, which makes a materially different card: Meloku is played as a repeatable engine precisely because the lands come back and can be replayed, and a sacrifice version would strip-mine its own mana base. Substituting it would silently change the card. The `return_to_hand` **op** is in the vocabulary but is an effect, not a cost: effects run on resolution, so the ability could be activated with no land on the battlefield at all, the payment would not gate activation, and it would not be rewindable if it failed. Same need already filed under this slug for Trench Behemoth (`data/authoring/gaps/trench_behemoth.json`), whose ability has no mana component; one cost field satisfying both is the work item.
- **(cost)** a cost component that returns a permanent you control to its owner's hand as part of paying an activated ability, chosen by an ordinary selector, e.g. `{"return_to_hand": {"zone": "battlefield", "controller": "you", "types": ["Land"], "count": 1}}`. It needs both halves of the existing cost contract: a payability test (a matching permanent exists, exactly as `_sacrifice_pool` gates `sacrifice`) and a payment step that asks the controller which permanent goes and then moves it to its owner's hand. Note this ability has no mana and no tap in its cost, so the returned permanent is the entire cost -- a bounce cost is the whole activation, not a rider on one.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `Cost` carries exactly `mana`, `tap`, `untap`, `sacrifice` (+`discard`, `discard_selector`, `discard_self`, `pay_life`, `remove_counters`, `exile_from_graveyard`) and nothing moves a battlefield permanent to hand. `sacrifice` is the closest -- it already takes the right selector shape and already asks the player to choose -- but it destroys the land instead of returning it, which is a materially different card: Trench Behemoth is a recursion engine precisely because the land comes back and can be replayed for another landfall trigger. Substituting it would silently change the card. The `return_to_hand` **op** exists but is an effect, not a cost: effects run on resolution after the ability is already on the stack, so paying with it would let the ability be activated with no land at all and would not be rewindable if the payment failed.

## spell-cost-reduction

Blocks **2** cards.

- **(static_effect)** a static ability on a permanent that reduces the generic portion of the cost of OTHER spells its controller casts, scoped by a filter over the spell's own printed characteristics - e.g. `{"kind": "static", "effect": "spell_cost_reduction", "affects_spells": {"controller": "you", "types": ["Creature"], "keywords": ["flying"]}, "amount": {"const": 1}}`. It must be read at the same choke points the existing self-reduction is (`legality.affordable`/`legality` cast enumeration and `game.cast` via `costs.cost_reduction`), so a spell offered at the reduced price is also paid at the reduced price, and it must be clamped at zero and generic-only like the existing one.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: The nearest thing is the card-level `cost_reduction` field (`carddef.CardDef.cost_reduction`, `costs.cost_reduction`, `loader.COST_REDUCTION_KEYS = {count, total_power}`), and it points the other way: it reduces the cost of the card that CARRIES it, and its filter is a board filter counting permanents on the battlefield (`costs._reduction_matches` iterates `state.battlefield`). Warden reduces the cost of a different card - a creature spell with flying being cast from hand - selected by that spell's own characteristics, which `cost_reduction` has no way to name and no way to apply to anything but its own card. Writing `cost_reduction` on Warden would make Warden itself cheaper, a different card. The static vocabulary offers no alternative either: `loader.STATIC_EFFECTS` is buff / grant_keyword / set_pt / add_subtype / set_types / protection plus the player-wide extra_land_drops, no_hand_limit, play_lands_from_graveyard, play_lands_from_library_top, double_land_triggers, double_land_mana, freeze_opponent_lands - all of which describe a characteristic of a permanent or a permission of a player, none of which touches what a spell costs. The `double_land_mana` precedent shows the shape a payment-time static takes, but it doubles mana produced by lands, not the price of a spell.
- **(selector)** a filter form that can be matched against a spell being cast (a card in hand / on the stack) rather than against a permanent on the battlefield, reading its printed types and keywords - so "creature spells with flying" is expressible at the moment legality prices the card
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `STATIC_FILTER_KEYS` (which `_validate_cost_reduction` reuses) does carry `types` and `keywords`, but the only consumer, `costs._reduction_matches`, walks `state.battlefield` and calls `chars(state, oid)` on permanents - there is no code path that applies a filter to the card whose cost is being computed. A trigger-based stand-in (`spell_cast` with `filter: {types: ["Creature"], keywords: ["flying"]}`) cannot substitute: the trigger resolves after the spell has already been cast and paid for, so at best it could refund mana into the pool, which is not the same as being able to afford the spell in the first place and would change what `legality` offers.
- **(static_effect)** a static ability on a permanent that reduces the generic cost of OTHER spells its controller casts, scoped by a filter over the spell's own printed characteristics (here: types include Creature and keywords include flying) and by who is casting it - e.g. `{"kind": "static", "effect": "spells_cost_less", "affects_spells": {"controller": "you", "types": ["Creature"], "keywords": ["flying"]}, "amount": {"const": 1}}`. Legality and payment must both read it by scanning the battlefield for such statics while deciding what is castable, the same generic-only, clamped-at-zero arithmetic `costs.cost_reduction` already does.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: The near miss is the card-level `cost_reduction` field, and it points the other way: `costs.cost_reduction(state, pid, card)` reads `card.cost_reduction` off the card BEING CAST and discounts that one card by counting permanents on the board (`{"count": filter}` / `{"total_power": filter}`). It is Ghalta - 'THIS spell costs {X} less' - and there is no form of it that reaches out to discount other spells, nor any filter position that reads the characteristics of the spell being cast rather than of battlefield permanents. Putting `cost_reduction` on Watcher of the Spheres would make Watcher itself cheaper, which is a different card. Nothing else covers it either: `STATIC_EFFECTS` in `cards/loader.py` holds only characteristic effects (buff, grant_keyword, set_pt, add_subtype, set_types, protection) and player-wide facts (extra_land_drops, no_hand_limit, play_lands_from_graveyard, play_lands_from_library_top, double_land_triggers, double_land_mana, freeze_opponent_lands) - none of which touch cost. The `replacements` whitelist is only `self_enters` / `self_enters_tapped` / `self_enters_with_counters`, so a cost-altering replacement cannot be written. A `spell_cast` triggered ability is too late by construction: the spell is already paid for and on the stack, and `mana_restriction` only filters which sources may pay, never how much is owed.

## ascend

Blocks **1** card.

- **(engine)** the city's blessing as a per-player, one-way, permanent designation (rule 702.131 / 700.6): a field on `PlayerState` such as `has_city_s_blessing: bool`, set the moment its controller controls ten or more permanents and never unset -- it survives the permanents leaving, survives the source of the Ascend ability leaving the battlefield, and is shared by every card that player controls, so a second Ascend card printed later reads the blessing that a first card granted. Needs three parts: (a) the player-state field itself; (b) the continuous check, which is a STATE TRIGGER, not a triggered ability -- it is checked whenever state-based actions are, uses no stack and cannot be responded to, so it belongs in the state-based-action pass in `engine/` next to the existing legend-rule/lethal-damage checks, gated on the controller of a permanent (or resolving spell) with the Ascend ability; and (c) card-level vocabulary to say the permanent has Ascend at all -- most plausibly a card field like `"ascend": true`, since it is a one-word keyword ability with no parameters, and since making it a `Keyword` enum member would wrongly put it in the derived keyword list that `grant_keyword` and evasion checks read
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `PlayerState` (`src/automtg/engine/player.py:20-65`) stores life, zones, mana, land drops, commander tax/damage, loss and UI flags -- there is no general per-player flag, designation or counter of any kind, so the blessing has nowhere to live and no value expression or condition can read it back. The closest one-way flag in the engine is `monstrous` (`engine/objects.py:46-48`, set by the `monstrosity` op at `effects/ops_board.py:252`), and it is wrong in all three respects that matter here: it lives on an OBJECT, so it is cleared by `reset_permanent_state` on any zone change and cannot be shared between two cards; it is set by an op resolving from the stack rather than by a continuous check; and there is no op-driven route to a player-wide equivalent, because none of the 46 ops writes durable player state. Nor can a triggered ability substitute. The `if` op's condition language CAN count permanents -- `{"cmp": ">=", "left": {"count": {"controller": "you"}}, "right": {"const": 10}}` is well-formed -- but every available trigger event fires on a discrete happening (`self_enters`, `permanent_enters`, `upkeep`, ...), and Ascend is not an event: a player who is at nine permanents when this creature enters and reaches ten by playing a land gets the blessing at the instant of the tenth, with no trigger of this card's having fired, and gets it during an opponent's turn just as readily. A trigger-plus-counter version would also be a DIFFERENT card in the direction that matters, since the blessing is never lost and a re-checked trigger would come and go. The seven player-wide statics (`effect: "extra_land_drops"`, `no_hand_limit`, `play_lands_from_graveyard`, `play_lands_from_library_top`, `double_land_triggers`, `double_land_mana`, `freeze_opponent_lands`, `docs/card-dsl.md` "Player-wide statics") are the only things in the DSL that describe a player rather than a characteristic, and each is an unconditional permission read live off the battlefield for as long as its source is there -- none of them SETS anything, and all of them stop when the source leaves, which is the opposite of "for the rest of the game"

Filtering any of these with `filter`/`condition` cannot help: the shortfall is that the moment being described never becomes an event, not that the event is too broad.

Concretely, the same three-step plumbing that already exists for X: record it on the object as it resolves (`GameObject.cast_x` at objects.py:77, set at stack.py:193 by `obj.cast_x = item.x`), carry it into the trigger's bindings (triggers.py:380 already does `"x": obj.cast_x`), and set it on the ability's EffectContext (stack.py:250 `_resolve_ability`, mirroring the `kicked=item.kicked` that stack.py:185 `_resolve_spell` already passes). This is the whole of what this card needs -- every other piece is already shipped, including the `kicker` cost field, the `{"kicked": true}` condition, the `self_enters` trigger event and the `not_subtypes` selector key the bounce half wants.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `{"kicked": true}` is the right condition and the loader will happily accept it here -- `_mentions_kicked` (loader.py:278-281) walks each ability's effects and its trigger condition, so the card passes the half-a-kicker check and loads clean. It is then silently inert: `stack._resolve_ability` builds its EffectContext without a `kicked=` argument, so `EffectContext.kicked` (context.py:37) falls back to its `False` default and `conditions.evaluate`'s `ctx.kicked == bool(cond["kicked"])` (conditions.py:62-63) is false on every resolution, kicked or not. The bounce would never happen, which is exactly the quietly-wrong card a gap record exists to prevent -- and gate verification, which casts a kicker card *kicked* (verify.py:498), would see an unchanged board. Putting the effect in `spell_effects`, where `kicked` genuinely works, is not open: Slinn Voda is a permanent and the loader routes a permanent's effects to `abilities`. Nothing else records how a permanent was cast either -- `StackItem.kicked` is documented as decided at cast time and read on resolution "because that is the only place it can be known: nothing about the object afterwards records what was paid for it" (structs.py:99-102), `zone_is` reads the source's current zone, and `cast_x` is the only cast-time value carried across the zone change. The bounce clause on its own is fully expressible -- `return_to_hand` over `{"zone": "battlefield", "types": ["Creature"], "not_subtypes": ["Merfolk", "Kraken", "Leviathan", "Octopus", "Serpent"], "count": "all"}`, the same shape already shipped on Whelming Wave -- but ungated it would fire on the unkicked {6}{U}{U} mode too, which is a strictly different card.

## landwalk

Blocks **1** card.

- **(keyword)** A parameterised landwalk keyword -- `islandwalk`, `swampwalk`, `forestwalk`, `mountainwalk`, `plainswalk` -- as members on `Keyword` (src/automtg/engine/enums.py), plus a check in `can_block` (src/automtg/engine/combat.py) that returns False when the attacker has landwalk of subtype X and the *defending player* controls at least one land with subtype X. The check must read the land's current subtypes via `chars()`, not the printed card, because this very card grants Island to everything; it belongs next to the existing flying/reach clause in `can_block`, which is already the one place block legality is decided. Because the family is five keywords sharing one rule, the cleanest shape is one keyword value carrying the land subtype (e.g. `landwalk:Island`) or a small keyword-to-subtype table consulted by the block check, so `grant_keyword` (op and static) picks up the whole family for free -- roughly 40 further landwalk cards sit in data/authoring/queue.json.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `reference.keywords` has no walk keyword at all, and the near-misses are all wrong. `menace` and `flying` are the only evasion in `can_block`, and both are unconditional properties of the attacker/blocker pair -- neither can express 'conditional on what the defending player's battlefield contains', and there is no static_filter_key or value expression that `can_block` consults. `hexproof`/`indestructible` are unrelated rules. Granting `flying` instead is a strictly different card: it would dodge every non-reach blocker regardless of the defender's lands, and would additionally satisfy this card's own third sentence for free. There is also no 'can't be blocked' effect in `ops` or `static_effects` to build a conditional unblockability on top of.

## may-pay

Blocks **1** card.

- **(cost)** an optional mana cost payable by the ability's controller while a triggered ability is resolving -- e.g. `{"op": "may", "pay": {"mana": "{2}"}, "effects": [{"op": "draw", "amount": {"const": 1}}]}` -- where the mana is actually paid out of the pool (with mana abilities activatable to make it) and the wrapped effects happen only when the payment completes
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: Every cost in reference is attached to the object being cast or activated, never to an effect mid-resolution: `Cost` (engine/carddef.py) carries mana, tap, untap, sacrifice, discard, discard_self, pay_life, remove_counters and exile_from_graveyard, and it is only ever read when a spell is cast or an ability is activated. The trigger here fires on its own and its effects run with no cost hook at all, so the {2} would simply have to be dropped -- turning a card that draws for {2} a land into one that draws free
- **(decision)** the yes/no prompt for that optional payment must be priced: offered only when the player can actually afford {2}, and its answer must be readable as the condition for the 'If you do' branch, so declining or being unable to pay skips the draw
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `may` (engine/effects/ops_control.py) is the only optional-effect op and it asks a bare yes/no with nothing at stake -- it takes `player`, `prompt`, `condition`, `effects`, `else` and `repeat`, but no cost, and it never consults affordability. Its `condition` and the `if` op both evaluate board conditions, and no condition in the vocabulary can read whether a mana payment was made, so 'If you do' has no source of truth to branch on. The nearest existing shape, `unless_pays` (Rhystic Study), is a different mechanic: it routes the payment to another player and inverts the outcome

## unless-pays

Blocks **1** card.

- **(decision)** an 'unless that player pays <cost>' wrapper on a triggered ability's effect: while the ability resolves, a player other than the ability's controller is offered an optional cost, and the wrapped effect happens only if they decline
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `may` is the only optional-effect op in reference and it asks the ability's own controller whether to apply the effect; it has no cost attached and cannot route the decision to the opponent whose spell triggered the ability, so the whole 'unless' branch would have to be dropped
- **(cost)** a mana cost ({1}) payable during another player's ability resolution by a player who does not control that ability, with the payment outcome (paid / not paid) readable as a condition

## untap-during-each-untap-step

Blocks **1** card.

- **(static_effect)** A continuous ability, read by the untap-step turn-based action, that adds a set of permanents chosen by an ordinary static filter to the set untapped during a *different* player's untap step. Concretely a static of the shape `{"kind": "static", "effect": "untap_during_others_untap_step", "affects": {"controller": "you", "types": ["Creature"], "colors": ["G", "U"]}}`, and a matching read inside `primitives.untap_all` (`src/automtg/engine/primitives.py:437-460`): today it walks the battlefield and skips every object whose `controller != pid`, so it must additionally untap any object matched by an active static of this kind whose controller is not the active player. The filter is the existing static selector (`characteristics._matches` -> the selector walk at `characteristics.py:270-300`), where `colors` is already an intersection test -- `if colors and not (set(colors) & card.colors)` at line 284-286 -- so `["G", "U"]` means exactly the printed "green and/or blue". This one effect covers the whole family at once: Seedborn Muse, Prophet of Kruphix, Awakening, Murkfiend Liege and Vedalken Orrery-adjacent 'untaps during each untap step' text all differ only in the filter.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `static_effects` is limited to `buff`, `grant_keyword`, `set_pt`, `add_subtype` and `extra_land_drops`. The first four write characteristics that the characteristics pipeline reads; `extra_land_drops` writes a player permission that the land-play legality check reads. None of them is read anywhere near the untap step. `skip_untap` is the closest existing vocabulary -- it is the *only* thing in the reference block that touches the untap step at all -- and it is the exact negation of what is wanted: it sets a one-shot `skip_next_untap` flag on an object, consumed by `untap_all` (`primitives.py:450-455`) to *remove* a permanent from an untap it would otherwise get. There is no positive counterpart, and no amount of skipping can add a permanent to an untap step that never considered it: `untap_all` is called from `turn._untap_step` (`turn.py:110-118`) as `untap_all(state, player.pid)` with the active player's pid hard-wired, so permanents controlled by anyone else are filtered out before any flag is consulted.
- **(trigger_event)** An `untap_step` trigger event, fired for the untapping player and honouring the existing `controller: "opponent"` clause, plus priority plumbing so an ability that triggers there can actually resolve during that step. This is the near-miss route -- 'at the beginning of each other player's untap step, untap all green and/or blue creatures you control' -- and it is written down because it is the first thing anyone will reach for; see below for why it is second best even once it exists.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: Three separate stops, all verified in the source. (1) There is no event: `TRIGGER_EVENTS` (`src/automtg/engine/triggers.py:28-47`) maps `upkeep`, `draw_step`, `begin_combat` and `end_step` and nothing for the untap step. (2) Nothing is even emitted for triggers to match: `turn.begin_step` handles `Step.UNTAP` by calling `_untap_step`, which uses `state.emit(EventType.TURN_BEGAN, ...)` rather than `triggers.fire(...)` (`turn.py:34-35`, `110-118`) -- `emit` records the event but never calls `collect`, so no ability is scanned during that step, and `TURN_BEGAN` is not in `TRIGGER_EVENTS` either. (3) Even with both fixed, the timing would be wrong: `step_grants_priority` returns `False` for `Step.UNTAP` (`turn.py:186-189`, correct per rule 502.3), so a queued triggered ability would sit in `pending_triggers` until the upkeep and untap one step late -- and worse, it would be respondable, which the printed card is not. Murkfiend Liege's line is a static ability modifying a turn-based action, not a trigger; the `static_effect` need above is the shape that matches the card. `delay` cannot stand in either: its `DELAY_STEPS` whitelist (`turn.py:68-73`) has no untap entry, and a delayed trigger is one-shot and must be scheduled by something that already resolved, whereas this is a permanent, always-on modification of every other player's untap step.

## variable-mana-ability

Blocks **1** card.

- **(engine)** A mana ability whose output is a value expression evaluated when it is activated, rather than a constant fixed at load time. Concretely: let a mana ability carry an amount alongside its `mana` symbol -- e.g. `{"kind": "activated", "is_mana_ability": true, "cost": {"tap": true}, "effects": [{"op": "add_mana", "mana": "{G}", "amount": {"counters_on": {"counter": "+1/+1", "objects": {"self_only": true}}}}]}` -- and teach the places that read `Ability.mana_options` to ask the board instead of reading a tuple: `costs.activate_mana_ability` (`engine/costs.py:497-520`, which must multiply the unit tuple by the evaluated amount when it pays out), the payment solver's source enumeration (`engine/costs.py:106-125` and `:151`, `:193`, so it counts the real number of {G} available rather than one), and `engine/legality.py:542-566` (so the client's mana row and its per-option labels are not a lie). The count must be read at activation time, and the value language already computes it: `{"counters_on": ...}` is in `VALUE_KEYS` (`engine/effects/values.py:44`, evaluated at lines 78-87) and reads live counters off the source. The same change unblocks every "Add {C} for each ..." card at once -- Gaea's Cradle, Cabal Coffers, Serra's Sanctum, Priest of Titania, Circle of Dreams Druid, Overgrown Battlement, Magus of the Coffers, Cloudpost and Kydele are all sitting in `data/cards/auto/templates.cards.json` today with a flat one-pip `add_mana`, i.e. approximated, so this is a correctness fix for nine shipped cards as well as an unblock for this one.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: A mana ability's output is a constant computed at load time and the effect interpreter is never run for it. `loader._sum_mana` (`cards/loader.py:595-607`) walks the ability's effects and raises `DslError` on anything that is not `add_mana`, folding the `mana` strings into one fixed 6-tuple; `loader._mana_options` (lines 583-592) stores those tuples on the `Ability`. `costs.activate_mana_ability` (`engine/costs.py:497-520`) then pays out `mana_produced(ability.mana_options[option_index])` and never touches `ability.effects` -- its own docstring says the mana "comes straight from the ability's precomputed `mana_options` rather than from running its effects", because a mana ability must never stop to ask anything. There is no value expression anywhere on that path, so no amount of counters can change what a mana ability produces. Three near misses, all checked: (1) `add_mana_per` is the closest op and is wrong twice over -- `loader._sum_mana` rejects it outright inside a mana ability (verified: `probe_a.abilities[0]: mana abilities may only contain 'add_mana' (or a single 'choose_mode' of them), got 'add_mana_per'`), and even where it is legal it counts OBJECTS, `len(resolve_pool(ctx, spec.get("per")))` in `engine/effects/ops_mana.py:33`, so it can say "for each Forest you control" but has no way to ask how many counters sit on one permanent. (2) A `choose_mode` mana ability of `add_mana {G}`, `add_mana {G}{G}`, ... compiles to several fixed options (`loader._mana_options` lines 585-591) and the payment solver picks whichever one it likes with nothing checking the counters -- a Gyre Sage that taps for six on an empty board, i.e. strictly better than printed. (3) Dropping `is_mana_ability` and building the amount out of `repeat` + `add_mana` numerically works but stops being a mana ability: the solver-tap and offerable checks (`engine/costs.py:106-125`) both require the flag, so the ability would go on the stack, be invisible to the payment solver, and could never be activated during a payment -- which is the only thing this card's mana is for. `mana_restriction` is unrelated (it filters which sources may pay, never how much they make), and `cost_reduction` points at costs rather than production.
